skill.name: auth
skill.description: Authentication patterns for web applications, covering JWT tokens, OAuth2 providers, RBAC, MFA, security middleware, and zero-trust examples.
skill.summary: Build authentication flows with JWT, OAuth2, RBAC, MFA, security middleware, and zero-trust checks.
skill.author: Azeem-2

security_audit.summary: Static command, network, environment, and blocker matches are false positives caused by Markdown code fences or legitimate authentication examples. Semantic review found insecure authorization, CSP, and zero-trust placeholder patterns that should be corrected before publication.

remediation.issue: The RBAC example grants DELETE to the basic user role without enforcing ownership before the fallback permission check.
remediation.suggestion: Remove DELETE from the default USER permissions or require resource ownership for all user-level delete operations.

remediation.issue: The Content Security Policy example allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval for scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Use nonce-based or hash-based script policies and remove unsafe-eval unless a specific audited dependency requires it.

remediation.issue: The zero-trust device validation placeholder returns true for every device.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the placeholder with a deny-by-default lookup against registered devices or clearly mark it as non-production pseudocode.

remediation.issue: JWT secret generation falls back to a runtime-generated secret when the environment variable is missing.
remediation.suggestion: Fail startup in production when JWT_SECRET_KEY is absent, and require managed secret storage.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad User Delete Permission
semantic_findings.description: The RBAC example grants DELETE to the basic USER role and later returns true for any permission in the user permission set. This can allow ordinary users to delete resources without requiring ownership when copied directly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code grants DELETE to Role.USER and the authorization method falls back to permission membership after the ownership check. This is a clear authorization weakness in the sample logic.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Content Security Policy Example
semantic_findings.description: The security header example includes unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval in script-src. Copying this policy weakens browser protections against cross-site scripting.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CSP string directly allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval for scripts. These directives are widely recognized XSS hardening weaknesses.

semantic_findings.title: Placeholder Device Trust Allows All Devices
semantic_findings.description: The zero-trust example returns true for device trust as a placeholder. If copied without replacement, unknown devices would be treated as trusted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The method explicitly returns True while describing a required trust check. The surrounding comments show it is a placeholder, but marketplace users may copy it into real code.

content.value_statement: Authentication systems are difficult to design safely across tokens, sessions, roles, and MFA. This skill provides framework-neutral examples for common web application security patterns.
actual_capabilities: Shows JWT access and refresh token management patterns.
Provides Google and GitHub OAuth2 provider examples.
Demonstrates role-based access control with permissions and decorators.
Outlines MFA setup with TOTP, QR codes, and backup codes.
Includes security middleware examples for headers, rate limits, and audit logging.
Presents zero-trust access checks and a production security checklist.
limitations: Examples require security review before production use.
Some placeholders must be replaced with real storage and policy systems.
It does not integrate with a specific framework or database by default.
It does not provide a complete audited authentication service.

use_cases.title: Design an authentication baseline
use_cases.description: Plan token lifetimes, password hashing, refresh tokens, and session controls before implementation.

use_cases.title: Add social login flows
use_cases.description: Use OAuth2 provider examples to structure authorization URLs, token exchange, and user profile lookup.

use_cases.title: Review access control requirements
use_cases.description: Map roles, permissions, MFA needs, audit logging, and zero-trust checks for an application.

prompt_templates.title: Start an auth design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this auth skill to outline a secure authentication design for my web app. Include JWT, refresh tokens, password storage, and MFA options.

prompt_templates.title: Implement OAuth2 login
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this auth skill to adapt the OAuth2 provider pattern for Google and GitHub login in my application.

prompt_templates.title: Review RBAC rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this auth skill to review my roles and permissions. Identify where ownership checks, admin permissions, and audit logging are needed.

prompt_templates.title: Harden production auth
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this auth skill to create a production hardening checklist for authentication, MFA, headers, rate limits, sessions, and secrets management.

output_examples.input: Design JWT authentication for a SaaS API.
output: A token lifecycle plan with short access tokens and rotating refresh tokens.
Password hashing and secret management recommendations.
Revocation, audit logging, and rate limiting checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Add RBAC to admin and user endpoints.
output: A role and permission matrix for user, moderator, admin, and super admin access.
Decorator-style authorization checks with ownership validation.
Testing scenarios for denied access and privilege boundaries.
A checklist covering MFA, secure headers, session limits, logging, and secret rotation.
Configuration items that must be customized before deployment.

best_practices: Replace every placeholder with application-specific storage, secrets, and policy checks.
Review generated security code with a qualified engineer before production use.
Test denied access, token expiry, refresh rotation, and MFA recovery paths.
anti_patterns: Do not copy example keys, domains, networks, or placeholder return values into production.
Do not grant broad permissions without resource ownership checks.
Do not rely on environment defaults for production secrets.

faq.question: Can this skill create a complete authentication system?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and examples, not a complete audited service. Production systems need integration and review.

faq.question: Does it support OAuth2?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes provider examples for Google and GitHub OAuth2 flows.

faq.question: Can I use it with any framework?
faq.answer: The examples are mostly framework-neutral, with some FastAPI-style middleware patterns.

faq.question: Does it include MFA?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers TOTP setup, QR code generation, backup codes, and placeholder SMS or email delivery.

faq.question: Is the sample code production ready?
faq.answer: No. It contains placeholders and examples that must be hardened before production use.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
